config.title: Form Validation with Zod + React Hook Form

intro.title: Form Validation with Zod + React Hook Form
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a user registration form with real-time validation feedback. You'll learn how to combine React Hook Form for efficient form state management with Zod, a powerful schema validation library, to define and enforce your form's rules. The core programming concept is schema-based validation, which ensures data integrity by checking user input against a predefined set of rules. You'll implement this by creating a Zod schema, integrating it with React Hook Form's `useForm` hook, and displaying validation errors to the user. This approach keeps your form logic clean, type-safe, and easy to maintain.
intro.usecase: Form validation with Zod and React Hook Form is essential for any application that collects user data, from simple contact forms to complex multi-step registration processes. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce checkout flows where shipping addresses and payment details must be validated before submission, or in SaaS dashboards where users configure account settings with specific format requirements. Developers implement these validation libraries to ensure data integrity while providing immediate, user-friendly feedback when inputs don't meet business rules. This approach prevents invalid data from reaching your backend while creating polished, professional user experiences across signup forms, profile editors, and data entry interfaces.

objectives: Initialize React Hook Form with Zod integration for form state management
Construct Zod schemas to define validation rules for form fields
Bind form inputs to React Hook Form using register and validation schemas
Render validation error messages based on Zod schema violations
Configure form submission handlers to process validated data
Manipulate form state to reset or update values after validation
Integrate Zod validation with custom form components and input types

steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of your file to bring in the necessary libraries for building forms with validation.

steps.title: Define the Zod validation schema
steps.instruction: Create a Zod schema object named 'formSchema' that validates a name (required, minimum 2 characters) and email (required, valid email format). Place this schema above your FormComponent.
steps.hint: Use z.object() to define the schema structure, then chain .string(), .min(2) for name, and .email() for email validation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zod schema object named 'formSchema' is created with validation rules for name and email fields.
successCriteria: The 'formSchema' object is defined using z.object() with name and email fields, each having appropriate validation methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both name and email fields have the correct validation methods (min() for name, email() for email).
steps.feedbackWrong: The schema isn't quite right. Remember to use z.object() with name and email fields, each with appropriate validation chains.

steps.title: Initialize React Hook Form with validation resolver
steps.instruction: Inside your FormComponent, call the useForm hook and configure it to use the Zod resolver with your schema. Store the result in a variable named 'form'.
steps.hint: Call useForm with an object containing a resolver property set to zodResolver(schema).
steps.expectedOutcome: The useForm hook is properly configured with the Zod resolver, ready for form validation.
successCriteria: useForm is called with a resolver configuration
zodResolver is passed the schema
The result is stored in a variable named 'form'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're passing the resolver configuration to useForm and storing the result in a variable named 'form'.
steps.feedbackWrong: call useForm with a resolver configuration that uses zodResolver with your schema.

steps.instruction: Inside your FormComponent, add a useState hook to store form submission results. Initialize it with null.
steps.hint: Call useState with an initial value of null and destructure the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:

const [submittedData, setSubmittedData] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a state variable ready to store form submission data.
successCriteria: A useState hook is added inside FormComponent with an initial value of null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with null as the initial value inside the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to add a useState hook inside FormComponent to store submission data.

steps.hint: The handleSubmit function should be defined inside the component and use the setSubmissionResults function to update the state with the formData.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleSubmit function is defined and ready to process validated form data.
successCriteria: A function named handleSubmit is defined inside the component

steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your FormComponent, add an input field for the 'name' property. Use the register function from React Hook Form to connect it to your validation schema, and display any validation errors below the input.
steps.hint: Use the register function with the field name 'name'. Access errors from the formState object to conditionally show error messages.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a name input field that shows validation errors when the field is empty or invalid.
successCriteria: An input field for 'name' is added with register('name'), and validation errors are displayed conditionally using errors.name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add the submit button and wire form submission
steps.instruction: Add a submit button inside the form and connect the form's onSubmit to the formHandleSubmit function with your submitForm handler.
steps.hint: Use the handleSubmit function from react-hook-form (aliased as formHandleSubmit) and pass your submitForm handler to it. Add a submit button with type='submit'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: form with submit button
<form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}>
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a submit button that triggers validation and submission when clicked.
successCriteria: A submit button with type='submit' is added inside the form
The form's onSubmit is connected to formHandleSubmit(submitForm)

steps.feedbackWrong: The submit button or form submission wiring is missing. Check that you've added a button with type='submit' and connected the form's onSubmit to formHandleSubmit(submitForm).
